text.en:
Keyd is the keyboard for Folio. It is a separate app because Android requires a keyboard to be its own input method, so the launcher can't contain one.

It types, corrects, learns, suggests, expands shortcuts, does emoji, splits around the fold, and speaks six languages: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese, each with its own keys, accents and word list.

**It asks for no permissions at all**, including no Internet permission. That isn't a promise in a privacy policy: Android enforces it. The word list is on the phone and the lookup is on the phone, so nothing it sees can leave, because it has no way to send anything.

Autocorrect only fixes clear typos, never a real word, and one backspace always undoes it. The suggestion strip agrees with what autocorrect would do. Words you type that no dictionary knows are learned on the phone, never from a password field and never from an app that asks it not to. Swearing is never corrected into another word.

items.en: Splits around the crease on a book fold, so no key sits on the hinge
Suggestions, a spell check, and autocorrect for clear typos only
Six languages, each with its own keys, accents and words
Accents on a long press, printed in the corner of the key
Clipboard history: never from a password field, forgotten after an hour unless pinned
Shortcuts: omw for on my way, and your own
Flick a key for what's printed on it; swipe the space bar to move the cursor
Emoji in your phone's own font
Light, dark or the system's, and a high-contrast option
No permissions, and no Internet permission

notes.en: Hold the globe for your languages and the period for symbols, swipe two fingers to undo, and an emoji at the end of the strip. Gesture tips, hold delay and backspace speed, and shift with backspace deletes forward. Contractions are ranked by how often each is typed, and Undo comes back for installs that had a 0.3.0 beta.

Emoji search, next-word prediction, contractions, and a strip that offers to keep a word or always fix it. Per-app settings, swipe up on Z X C V A to edit, slide from shift to select, a toolbar you arrange, one-handed mode, vibration strength and pure black. Fewer wrong fixes, accents offered instead of forced, and typos no longer learned.

Fixes the keyboard staying fullscreen after you hid it (thanks, Roby). Adds a cursor pad, a voice key that hands you to your phone's voice keyboard, Folio, Material and Samsung key styles, pinned clips as text shortcuts, Report a problem with a preview of every line, and export and import of what it learned.

The top of Settings says whether Keyd is on and chosen, with the button that fixes the missing step. About shows the version, what's new and where to report a problem. The gear in Android's keyboard list opens Settings.
The first release: typing, corrections, learning, shortcuts, emoji, clipboard history, the split around the fold, and six languages.
